answer: The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust: influence equals account age multiplied by honest epochs, so reputation accrues like moss on shale — slowly, only under verifiable load. Fresh identities are tundra: vast but barren, unable to move capital or votes until seasons pass. An attacker must keep thousands of dormant accounts live, honest, and fee-paying for months, with every slashing event resetting a lineage to zero; the nectar of early influence never flows to bots, so mass identity forgery costs more than it can ever extract.
